game: Game Terms (so far only Heroes) and Patches.\n\nA Hero is a Game Term with an official Chinese and an official English name.\nIts URL slug is derived from the English Official name.\n\nAnything the console should refuse raises `Refused` with a message to show.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\n\nclass Refused(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A Hero or Patch change the console refuses, with the reason to show.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.message = message\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Hero:\n    id: int\n    name_zh: str\n    name_en: str\n    slug: str\n\n\ndef _hero_from_row(row: sqlite3.Row) -> Hero:\n    return Hero(id=row[\"id\"], name_zh=row[\"name_zh\"], name_en=row[\"name_en\"],\n                slug=row[\"slug\"])\n\n\ndef slugify(name_en: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"`Vanessa` -> `vanessa`, `Black Knight` -> `black-knight`.\"\"\"\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", name_en.lower()).strip(\"-\")\n\n\ndef add_hero(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, name_zh: str, name_en: str) -> Hero:\n    name_zh, name_en = name_zh.strip(), name_en.strip()\n    cur = conn.execute(\n        \"INSERT INTO game_terms (kind, name_zh, name_en, slug)\"\n        \" VALUES ('hero', ?, ?, ?)\", (name_zh, name_en, slugify(name_en)))\n    row = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM game_terms WHERE id = ?\",\n                       (cur.lastrowid,)).fetchone()\n    return _hero_from_row(row)\n\n\ndef heroes(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> list[Hero]:\n    rows = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM game_terms WHERE kind = 'hero'\"\n                        \" ORDER BY name_en COLLATE NOCASE\").fetchall()\n    return [_hero_from_row(row) for row in rows]\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Q3PxU84xQJfU3Z2cf81zJL","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/app/routes/game.py","content":"\"\"\"Heroes game\nfrom app.accounts import User\nfrom app.web import flash, redirect, signed_in_user, templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\n\n@router.get(\"/admin/heroes\")\ndef hero_list(request: Request, user: Annotated[User, Depends(signed_in_user)]):\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        heroes = game.heroes(conn)\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/heroes.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"英雄\", \"user\": user, \"heroes\": heroes})\n\n\n@router.post(\"/admin/heroes\")\ndef add_hero(request: Request, user: Annotated[User, Depends(signed_in_user)],\n             name_zh: Annotated[str, Form()], name_en: Annotated[str, Form()]):\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        hero = game.add_hero(conn, name_zh=name_zh, name_en=name_en)\n    flash(request, <tbody>\n    {% for hero in heroes %}\n      <tr><td>{{ hero.name_zh }}</td><td>{{ hero.name_en }}</td><td><code>{{ hero.slug }}</code></td></tr>\n    {% else %}\n      <tr><td Read Part 0 and Part 1 first.\n2. `docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md` — how you are graded. Read it **before** you build.\n3. `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` — Exercise A, in Part 4 of the manual.\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\nuv sync\ncp .env.example .env    # then change the passwords and the secret key\nuv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py   # one Admin, one Editor\nuv run --env-file .env cms serve   # then open http://localhost:8000/login\n```\n\nThe seeded accounts are `admin@example.test` (Admin, 演示管理员) and\n`editor@example.test` (Editor, 演示编辑), with the passwords you set in `.env` as\n`CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`. The seed script refuses to run\nwithout them; there are no default passwords.\n\n## What is here\n\n```text\n.claude/hooks/     the context meter and usage ledger (Exercise A lives in ctx_guard.py)\nscripts/           usage_report.py (Exercise B lives in spend()), check_submission.py, seed_demo.py\ntests/             the exercise tests, plus helpers such as client_as(\"editor\")\napp/, templates/   the T00 skeleton — every CMS feature is yours to build\ndocs/adr/          two example decision records\n```\n\nTwo functions are deliberately unfinished and their tests fail until you write them:\n`decide()` in `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` and `spend()` in `scripts/usage_report.py`.\nBoth are graded. Use `/tdd`, as the manual says.\n\n## Deadlines\n\nStage 1 (`mp2-mvp` tag): Tue Sep 29, 2:40 pm Eastern (soft target).\nStage 2 (`mp2-final` tag): Tue Oct 6, 2:40 pm Eastern, grace until Wed Oct 7, 2:40 pm.\n\nRun `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` before you submit.\n\n## Generative AI Use Statement\n\n*(Required. Replace this section: name the models and skills you used, quote two\nprompts you really sent, describe one real model failure, and include a\n\"Backends used\" table if you ever switched providers.)*","is_error":false}]}}

If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review uncommitted changes since HEAD (c868270) against ticket #3 (T02 — Admins manage Heroes and Patches) and spec #1. Exclude notes/usage-ledger.csv and docs/transcripts/."}]}}

Also the system-level rule: code should read like the surrounding code (comment density, naming, idiom).\n\nSmell baseline (Fowler, Refactoring ch.3). The repo overrides; each smell is always a judgement call, never a hard violation:\n- Mysterious Name: a name that doesn't reveal what it does or holds → rename.\n- Duplicated Code: same logic shape in more than one hunk/file → extract shared shape.\n- Feature Envy: method reaching into another object's data more than its own → move it.\n- Data Clumps: same few fields/params travelling together → bundle into a type.\n- Primitive Obsession: primitive/string standing in for a domain concept → small type.\n- Repeated Switches: same switch/if-cascade on same type recurs → polymorphism or shared map.\n- Shotgun Surgery: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files → gather.\n- Divergent Change: one module edited for several unrelated reasons → split.\n- Speculative Generality: abstraction/params/hooks for needs the spec doesn't have → delete.\n- Message Chains: long a.b().c().d() navigation → hide behind one method.\n- Middle Man: function that mostly delegates → cut it.\n- Refused Bequest: subclass ignoring most of what it inherits → composition.\n\nBrief: Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found no blocking spec gaps. Every acceptance criterion in ticket #3 is implemented, and the T02 tests pass (25 passed).\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n\n- None blocking. A few things are only half-covered:\n  - **Patch duplicates.** \"A Patch that already exists is refused.\" The only check is an exact-text match after trimming spaces. So `6.7`, `v6.7` and `6.70` are three different Patches, and any text such as `abc` is accepted. This meets the wording but is weak.\n  - **Correcting a Patch.** \"the newest Patch becomes the Current Patch\". There is no way to edit or delete a Patch. A mistyped Patch becomes the Current Patch and stays there. The ticket doesn't ask for editing, but story 64 (\"a balance patch takes one action on my side\") assumes the Admin can recover from a typo.\n  - **Later stories.** Story 15 (Editors pick from the Current Patch plus the two before it) and story 65 (Current Patch in the public site header) belong to later tickets, so I'm not counting them here.\n\n**(b) Not asked for (mild)**\n\n- `game_terms` already allows all seven kinds (`CHECK kind IN ('hero', 'item', …)`). That looks ahead to story 58 (\"manage Game Terms of seven kinds\"), which this ticket doesn't cover. It is schema only, but it fixes a design choice early.\n- It refuses an English name that has no letters or digits, because no slug can be made from it. This is a reasonable rule, but the ticket doesn't state it.\n- Smaller additions: \"英雄 / 版本\" links in the console nav (Admins only), a 404 for a Hero that doesn't exist, trimming of names, and README edits. All harmless.\n\n**(c) Implemented, but possibly wrong**\n\n- **Slug changes on edit.** \"An Admin can edit a Hero's Official names\" and story 63's \"URL slug derived from its English Official name\". In `app/game.py` `edit_hero`, the slug is recalculated whenever the English name changes. That fits \"derived from\", but once Hero pages are published, one rename breaks every existing link to that Hero. Neither the spec nor the ticket says whether a slug stays fixed. This needs a decision now, before the site build ticket depends on it.\n- **\"Newest\" means \"added last\".** \"the newest Patch becomes the Current Patch\". In `app/db.py` and `game.patches`, the Current Patch is simply the highest row id. If an Admin later adds an older Patch they forgot, such as `6.5` after `6.7`, then `6.5` becomes the Current Patch. This matches the ticket's \"Adding a Patch … makes it the Current Patch\". It goes against CONTEXT.md's \"The newest Patch of the game\", if \"newest\" means the highest version number. Worth confirming which reading is meant.\n- **Editor refusal is correct.** \"An Editor is refused (redirect or 403) on every Hero and Patch management route, including by typing the URL.\" The router itself requires an Admin (`APIRouter(dependencies=[Depends(admin_user)])`) and refuses Editors with a 403. Editors who haven't finished first-login setup are redirected to setup first. Both are allowed outcomes. I found no defect.\n- **Slug uniqueness is correct.** \"A Hero's slug … is unique.\" It is checked in the app and also enforced by `UNIQUE (kind, slug)` in the database. It is unique among Heroes only, not across all Game Terms, which is fine for this ticket.\n\nThe files involved are `app/game.py`, `app/routes/game.py`, `app/web.py`, `app/db.py` and `scripts/seed_demo.py`, all in /Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>48871</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>4</tool_uses><duration_ms>45758</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

Sharing one class would mean editing T01 code for no change in behaviour. |\n| Three `*_page` helpers repeat `TemplateResponse(..., status_code=400 if error else 200)` | **Kept.** This matches the T01 `auth.py` pattern, and three short call sites don't justify a helper. |\n| `name_zh, name_en` travel together (Data Clumps) | **Kept.** It is mild and matches T01's keyword-argument style. Revisit when the other Game Term kinds arrive. |\n| The `kind = 'hero'` literal is repeated in SQL | **Kept.** Generalise when T-next adds the other six kinds, not before. |\n| `patches.created_at` is never read | **Kept.** Every table has `created_at` (`users`, `sessions`). |\n\n### Spec (every acceptance criterion met; 25 T02 tests pass)\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| Patch duplicates are caught by exact text only (`6.7`, `v6.7` and `6.70` all differ) | **Kept, as an open question.** The ticket only asks that an existing Patch be refused. A format rule (such as digits and dots only) can be a follow-up if wanted. |\n| There is no way to correct a mistyped Patch | **Out of scope** for T02, which doesn't ask for editing or deleting Patches. Candidate follow-up ticket. |\n| The `game_terms` CHECK already lists all seven kinds | **Kept.** `CONTEXT.md` defines Game Term as one of seven kinds, so the schema stores the concept rather than a Hero-only table. |\n| A slug is re-derived when the English name is edited | **Kept, as a decision to confirm.** It follows \"derived from its English Official name\", and no public Hero pages exist yet. Recorded in the glossary entry. Revisit before the Site build ticket publishes Hero URLs. |\n| \"Newest\" means \"added last\", so backfilling an older Patch would make it current | **Kept.** The ticket says \"Adding a Patch … makes it the Current Patch\". Flagged for confirmation. |\n| An English name with no letters or digits is refused | **Kept.** A slug can't be derived from it, so the alternative is a broken URL. |\n| The Editor refusal (router-level `Depends(admin_user)`, 403) and slug uniqueness (app check plus `UNIQUE (kind, slug)`) | Confirmed correct, no change. |\n\nTest run: all 25 T01/T02 tests pass (`test_t02_heroes_patches.py`, `test_t02_seed.py`, `test_t01_seed.py`), along with every other non-exercise test. The 14 remaining failures are the deliberately unimplemented Exercise A/B stubs (`test_ctx_guard.py`, `test_usage_report.py`), which T02 doesn't touch.\nEOF","description":"Post code-review findings comment on issue #3"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":584,"cache_read_input_tokens":121567,"output_tokens":1491,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":584,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1491,"cache_read_input_tokens":121567,"cache_creation_input_tokens":584,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":584},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_0182Ffrnf933pgUJ5Pzdt2KX":{"command":"gh issue comment 3 --body-file - {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"d96011e5-3b71-4963-9a6a-32eb66e9ffdb","hash":"1d4f85a35d0010358e59fb4e71e9858f230bbfd49eea8d3e7d0990a9873d53ca","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UunudBXvXCNHQZpUw4UHj8","type":"tool_result","content":"{\"base\":\"main\",\"body\":\"## T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\\n\\nCloses #2. The spec is #1.\\n\\n### What's in it\\n- **Login and logout.** Sign in with email and password; passwords are stored as argon2 hashes. Sessions live on the server, and the browser holds the session id in a signed cookie, so logging out ends the session even if someone copied the cookie.\\n- **CSRF.** Every POST in the app is checked for a CSRF token.\\n- **Refusals.** A wrong password and an unknown email get the same message and take the same time. Deactivated accounts see 账号已停用, and any session they already had open stops working.\\n- **First-login setup.** Someone with a temporary password must choose a new password and a unique Display name before reaching any other console page. Uniqueness ignores letter case.\\n- **Console shell.** A Chinese nav bar, a message after every save, and a dashboard at `/admin/dashboard` that greets by Display name. `/admin` stays the T00 hello page.\\n- **Seed.** `scripts/seed_demo.py` creates one Admin and one Editor from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`, and refuses to run without them.\\n- **Tests.** Each test gets a fresh SQLite database through `CMS_DATABASE`. `client_as()` now submits the login form's CSRF token.\\n\\n### Also in this PR\\n- The earlier notes and grill commits on this branch: the client brief, the field notes, the CMS vocabulary research, and the `CONTEXT.md` glossary.\\n- A merge of `origin/main` that keeps both sets of WordPress Playground field notes (10 from the branch, plus the 2 from `main` as notes 11 and 12).\\n- `.env.example` now quotes `CMS_SITE_TITLE`, because `uv run --env-file` rejected the unquoted value with spaces.\\n\\n### Verification\\n- `uv run pytest`: the 28 T00 + T01 tests pass. The 14 failures that remain are the course's unfinished exercises (`decide()`, `spend()`), which failed the same way before this ticket.\\n- `pyright` reports 0 errors.\\n- A live smoke test on uvicorn, seeded from `.env.example`, passed.\\n- The `/code-review` findings and how each was resolved are in a comment on #2.\\n\\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\\n\",\"commits\":[\"notes: field notes and client brief (The Bazaar Chinese community)\",\"notes: CMS vocabulary research (Part 2.3)\",\"grill: CONTEXT.md glossary for The Bazaar guide site\",\"T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\",\"Merge origin/main: keep both sets of WordPress Playground field notes\",\"T02: Admins manage Heroes and Patches\",\"T02: glossary — the Current Patch is the one added last\"],\"mergeable\":\"MERGEABLE\",\"title\":\"T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\"}","is_error":false}]}}

{"parentUuid":"d2097543-2ed4-482a-ad3b-47cec76a40ee","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b48530ff-acfd-40e9-9ff0-75008d2eafb3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01UunudBXvXCNHQZpUw4UHj8","type":"tool_result","content":"{\"base\":\"main\",\"body\":\"## T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\\n\\nCloses #2. The spec is #1.\\n\\n### What's in it\\n- **Login and logout.** Sign in with email and password; passwords are stored as argon2 hashes. Sessions live on the server, and the browser holds the session id in a signed cookie, so logging out ends the session even if someone copied the cookie.\\n- **CSRF.** Every POST in the app is checked for a CSRF token.\\n- **Refusals.** A wrong password and an unknown email get the same message and take the same time. Deactivated accounts see 账号已停用, and any session they already had open stops working.\\n- **First-login setup.** Someone with a temporary password must choose a new password and a unique Display name before reaching any other console page. Uniqueness ignores letter case.\\n- **Console shell.** A Chinese nav bar, a message after every save, and a dashboard at `/admin/dashboard` that greets by Display name. `/admin` stays the T00 hello page.\\n- **Seed.** `scripts/seed_demo.py` creates one Admin and one Editor from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`, and refuses to run without them.\\n- **Tests.** Each test gets a fresh SQLite database through `CMS_DATABASE`. `client_as()` now submits the login form's CSRF token.\\n\\n### Also in this PR\\n- The earlier notes and grill commits on this branch: the client brief, the field notes, the CMS vocabulary research, and the `CONTEXT.md` glossary.\\n- A merge of `origin/main` that keeps both sets of WordPress Playground field notes (10 from the branch, plus the 2 from `main` as notes 11 and 12).\\n- `.env.example` now quotes `CMS_SITE_TITLE`, because `uv run --env-file` rejected the unquoted value with spaces.\\n\\n### Verification\\n- `uv run pytest`: the 28 T00 + T01 tests pass. The 14 failures that remain are the course's unfinished exercises (`decide()`, `spend()`), which failed the same way before this ticket.\\n- `pyright` reports 0 errors.\\n- A live smoke test on uvicorn, seeded from `.env.example`, passed.\\n- The `/code-review` findings and how each was resolved are in a comment on #2.\\n\\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\\n\",\"commits\":[\"notes: field notes and client brief (The Bazaar Chinese community)\",\"notes: CMS vocabulary research (Part 2.3)\",\"grill: CONTEXT.md glossary for The Bazaar guide site\",\"T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\",\"Merge origin/main: keep both sets of WordPress Playground field notes\",\"T02: Admins manage Heroes and Patches\",\"T02: glossary — the Current Patch is the one added last\"],\"mergeable\":\"MERGEABLE\",\"title\":\"T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\"}","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"df55b175-3f94-4ef4-b49f-33c574d2050a","timestamp":"2026-10-17T12:37:29.866Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"{\"base\":\"main\",\"body\":\"## T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\\n\\nCloses #2. {"parentUuid":"6c0154c5-c2c7-49de-8867-f0006ff103a4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7pepytmUd8BLEwP1YWA","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Cew8esJgBQYAKYh17br86X","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/d96011e5-3b71-4963-9a6a-32eb66e9ffdb/scratchpad/pr13.md <<'EOF'\n## Summary\n\nTwo tickets: **T01** sign-in (closes #2) and **T02** Admins manage Heroes and Patches (closes #3). The spec is #1.\n\n```diff\n app/\n ├── accounts.py        # T01: users, argon2 hashes, sessions, first-login setup\n+├── game.py            # T02: Heroes (Game Terms with both Official names, Slug) and Patches\n ├── web.py             # T01: signed cookie, app-wide CSRF, flash, signed_in_user\n+│                      # T02: admin_user → 403 for Editors\n └── routes/\n     ├── auth.py        # T01: /login, /logout, /admin/setup\n     ├── dashboard.py   # T01: /admin/dashboard\n+    └── game.py        # T02: /admin/heroes, /admin/heroes/{id}/edit, /admin/patches\n```\n\n**T01:** sign in with email and password. A wrong password and an unknown email get the same refusal. Deactivated accounts are refused, and their open sessions stop working. A person with a temporary password must finish First-login setup (new password plus a unique Display name) before reaching any other page.\n\n**T02:** every Hero and Patch route sits behind a router-level `admin_user` dependency:\n\n```text\nadd_hero(name_zh, name_en)\n  refuse if either Official name is blank\n  slug = slugify(name_en)          # Vanessa → vanessa, Black Knight → black-knight\n  refuse if another Hero has slug\nedit_hero: same checks; the Slug follows a corrected English name\nadd_patch(name)\n  refuse if blank or already exists\n  → it is now the Current Patch    # the Patch added last, not the highest number\n```\n\n`scripts/seed_demo.py` creates one Admin and one Editor from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`, plus four demo Heroes and Patches 6.5–6.7 (6.7 current). Running it again changes nothing. `CONTEXT.md` gains a **Slug** entry and a sharper **Current Patch** definition, both confirmed by the client.\n\nAlso on this branch: the notes and grill commits (client brief, field notes, vocabulary research, the glossary), a merge of `origin/main` that keeps both sets of WordPress Playground field notes, and a quoted `CMS_SITE_TITLE` in `.env.example`.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- **Before (main):** none of these routes exist (`GET /admin/heroes` → 404), and the seed script doesn't exist.\n  **After:** `uv run pytest`: 53 passed.
